evidence.quote: Replication lag can build up when cluster nodes cannot reliably communicate with each other.
Secondary nodes can experience resource contention when they cannot efficiently handle incoming read operations from the primary. This can cause memory issues such as cache contention.
If a secondary node cannot flush dirty data to disk quickly enough, it falls behind the primary.
Causes include network latency, I/O bottlenecks on the secondary, or excessive write load on the primary.
High iowait combined with replication lag often means the secondary disk cannot keep up with oplog apply.
